chunks: From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī, who said:
I saw Abā Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام praying in a qamīṣ, having girded himself above it with a cloth, while he was praying.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِيَ: Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī, the ninth Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.اتَّزَرَ: he girded himself or wrapped a cloth around his waist
key_terms.بِمِنْدِيلٍ: with a cloth or kerchief used as a wrap
key_terms.فَوْقَهُ: over it, meaning over the qamīṣ
key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: a shirt or tunic worn as clothing

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to wear an izār or cloth over a qamīṣ during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report describes Abā Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام performing salat (prayer) while wearing a qamīṣ and girding a cloth over it. In the context of the chapter, it relates to the legal discussion of the karāhah (dislikedness) of wearing an izār over a shirt during prayer.
